summary: B79 restored the tin variety data, so the first residual is no longer the step-50 hunger stop. Eating the human wererat tin reaches C eat.c:cpostfx(), which sets u.ulycn; JS still skips were.c:set_ulycn. C then consumes the once-per-turn lycanthrope chance roll in allmain.c:moveloop_core(), a branch absent from the JS elapsed-turn path, producing the first residual RNG mismatch at step 50. Implementing the setter and chance branch is the required first-cause scope. The one remaining screen at step 77 is a later, separate potion.c:peffect_water() -> were.c:you_were() -> polyself.c:polymon() gap.

source.branch: After the turn upkeep, when the hero is not invulnerable, C clears stale mvl_change state and, absent a successful polymorph roll, tests `ismnum(u.ulycn) && !Upolyd && !rn2(80 - (20 * night()))`. A zero roll selects mvl_change=2 and may call you_were() when multi permits and the hero is not unchanging. This case eats a human wererat tin at step 50, so C first sets u.ulycn=PM_WERERAT; its recorded daytime roll is rn2(80)=73 and fails the shape-change check. JS lacks both the preceding setter and this hero lycanthropy chance branch; its rn2(20)=13 at the same RNG position consumes the raw draw C used for rn2(80)=73.
callers: C allmain.c:moveloop() loops through moveloop_core() (586-597); JS js/allmain.js:moveloop() invokes its moveloop_core() (1735-1749), reached from js/jsmain.js:runSegment(). The missing hero-state branch belongs in the elapsed-turn tail represented by js/allmain.js:finishElapsedTurnAfterTimeout() (929 onward).

The prerequisite state mutation is reached through C eat.c:consume_tin() -> cpostfx() -> were.c:set_ulycn(PM_WERERAT) (eat.c:1323-1325). JS js/eat.js:cpostfx() takes the same catch_lycanthropy branch but records set_ulycn and retouch_equipment as gaps (2746-2748).
dependencies: Required source scope also includes the complete were.c:set_ulycn() function (230-237): assign u.ulycn, then call set_uasmon() to refresh innate form properties, especially Drain_resistance. JS has polyself.c:set_uasmon() at js/polyself.js:539-616, but no were.c:set_ulycn implementation; the C eat.c caller currently skips it.

The allmain.c branch reads night(), the current polymorph/lycanthropy state, static mvl_change, multi, and Unchanging, then may call stop_occupation() or were.c:you_were(). For the observed case the rn2(80) result is nonzero, so these success-side effects are not taken at step 50.

C eat.c:cpostfx() calls artifact.c:retouch_equipment(2) immediately after set_ulycn(). JS currently records this as an unported gap and polyself.js retains a stub. It is a separate equipment-touch behavior and is not the owner of the first RNG mismatch; preserve it as an unresolved dependency instead of attributing the turn-roll defect to it.

The final unmatched screen requires the later cursed-water branch: C potion.c:peffect_water() at 740-745 calls were.c:you_were() when cursed water is drunk by an unpolymorphed lycanthrope; JS js/potion.js:1004-1009 records were.c:you_were as unported. C were.c:you_were() increments gw.were_changes and calls polyself.c:polymon(u.ulycn) (192-209). The recorded step 77 includes polymon RNG rn2(500)=112 and d(2,8)=12 and the screen says the hero turns into a wererat. Keep this as a separate downstream screen gap; it is not the step-50 first RNG cause.

nethack-c/patches/README.md describes deterministic runtime, stable sorting, PRNG logging, and screen capture. Search of nethack-c/patches for `ulycn`, `moveloop_core`, `set_ulycn`, and `you_were` returned no matches, so the gameplay behavior traced here comes from upstream C.

evidence: Current B79 queue entry `.cache/B79-final-work-queue.json` and evaluation `challenges/evaluations/20261001214251-v17.json` at commit 1f29dddb7791d0584379eeb425ef34791d600acc retain the same v17 manifest SHA-256 3b117af41e940caf724f6f5f5a65de625c20416854fadef002c0533aaaa57ada and recording SHA-256 70af4f5eb9759e70079659e627121d36a8b37b0bff0e19aa97b8839c08cc0d5e. The current queue has remainingScreens=1 and recordedSteps=78: 77/78 screens and cursors matched, while the earliest RNG difference is step 50, C rn2(80)=73 @ moveloop_core(allmain.c:328) versus JS rn2(20)=13.

Focused replay receipt `.cache/B79-orc-focused-replay.json` records the exact one-case command `node frozen/ps_test_runner.mjs --worker-session=challenges/cases/v17/orc-wizard-tin-lycanthropy-cursed-water-corrected-letters.session.json`, exit 0, and result 77/78 screens, 2682/2694 RNG calls, 77/78 cursors. This replay was run against the stated commit and did not create a C recording.

B79 immutable delivery packet referenced by `.cache/B79-delivery-packet.txt`, `context.postFixReplay` for this case and `checks[5]`, independently report 77/78 screens and the same first RNG divergence at step 50: C rn2(80)=73 in allmain.c:328 and JS rn2(20)=13. The prior accepted investigation was based on commit 45a483d2dd3320f9268aeb4477a785237e69df4e and evaluation `challenges/evaluations/20261001190602-v17.json` at 518d4526ccba82c89752a8babb892ba9bc48bc60; that record had 50/78 screens and stopped at step 50 in newuhs() because dried tin TIN_VARIETIES[7].nutrition was undefined. B79 restored the complete tintxts[] nutrition/greasy metadata, and the case now reaches the later cpostfx/allmain branch; the old hunger cause is superseded and must not be reintroduced as current scope.

Upstream `nethack-c/upstream/src/eat.c:1127-1327` sets catch_lycanthropy=PM_WERERAT for PM_HUMAN_WERERAT and at 1323-1325 calls set_ulycn() then retouch_equipment(2). The recorded step 47 selects dried variety index 7 (`rn2(15)=7 @ tin_variety(eat.c:1503)`); step 50 key y displays “You consume dried wererat.” and the rest of that C turn reaches `rn2(80)=73 @ moveloop_core(allmain.c:328)`.

Upstream `nethack-c/upstream/src/were.c:230-237` defines the complete setter as `u.ulycn = which; set_uasmon();`. C `allmain.c:307-339` then checks lycanthropy at 327-329 after upkeep and before searching/warning. In `js/allmain.js:929-1013`, the elapsed-turn tail moves from regeneration and the teleport branch to searching with no corresponding hero `u.ulycn`/`mvl_change` check. The focused search `rg -n "u\.ulycn|mvl_change|80 - \(20 \* night" js/allmain.js` returned no matches (exit 1). JS `cpostfx()` still calls `note_unported` for set_ulycn at `js/eat.js:2746-2748`; the existing `set_uasmon()` implementation is at `js/polyself.js:539-616`.

C `potion.c:740-745` and `were.c:192-209` explain the separate step-77 screen: cursed water calls you_were() for an unpolymorphed lycanthrope, which changes the hero to u.ulycn through polymon(). JS `potion.js:1004-1009` skips this call using `note_unported("were.c you_were")`. Recorded C step 77 contains d(2,6)=11, exercise RNG, then rn2(500)=112 and d(2,8)=12 in polymon and the “You turn into a wererat!” text; JS’s step-77 screen/cursor mismatch is therefore downstream of the new step-50 state/turn-roll cause.

Patch scope check: `nethack-c/patches/README.md` lists instrumentation changes for deterministic inputs, sorting, RNG logging, and captured screens. `rg -n "ulycn|moveloop_core|set_ulycn|you_were" nethack-c/patches` returned no matches, confirming the first-cause gameplay rules are from upstream C rather than a recorder patch.
